text:
Devon Levi's first career shutout came in the building where every hockey moment is magnified, and it ended the way you'd want it to: with Levi stopping Auston Matthews in the final seconds to keep it 1-0. The Oilers have won four straight. The Maple Leafs have lost six straight, all in regulation, and Daily Faceoff Toronto called it the worst homestand in the franchise's 109-year history.

This was a tight, careful game with almost nothing given away at even strength (1.05 expected goals to 1.03, the quality of chances), and on those chances Toronto won it in 52% of our replays. It was settled by the least likely shot of the night. At 15:34 of the second, Evan Bouchard's slap shot, a 2% chance, got through Anthony Stolarz off feeds from Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl. That moved Edmonton's win chance from 48% to 70%, and the assist stretched McDavid's point streak to 21 games.

Stolarz was the second star, 22 saves on 23, and deserved better. Levi stopped all 19 Toronto shots, 1.4 goals better than they usually allow, and that last save on Matthews was the biggest swing of the game. Nick Paul had Toronto's best look, a 15% chance in the second, and missed the net. The Leafs Nation's instant reaction summed it up from the home side: they held the league's best offensive team to one goal and still lost.

For Toronto, the questions are getting louder. Matthews has publicly backed Jim Hiller as the coach's seat gets warmer, William Nylander is answering trade rumours, and rookie Gavin McKenna is talking about his limited minutes. In Edmonton, the question is the opposite kind: whether Levi, the goalie Buffalo moved on from, is the answer the Oilers have been looking for in net for years. The Oilers play in Philadelphia tonight.
headline: Levi's first shutout deepens Toronto's worst homestand
